\section[(cum horologio)]{The same writing, with a clock}

\label{lesson:LA-W03-cum-horologio}



\begin{quote}
You wrote your own line with as long as you liked.

A task you can only do untimed is not yet a task you can do.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — timed production}
\textbf{What this track's contract publishes.} The Latin A1 writing paper runs \textbf{30 minutes} and holds \textbf{three} parts, which is one more than most:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item dictation and orthography — 5 items, \textbf{8 to 15 words};
  \item controlled sentences — 4 items, \textbf{20 to 35 words};
  \item a short personal note — 3 items, \textbf{35 to 50 words}.
\end{itemize}

Those numbers come out of \texttt{task-shapes/a1.json}, not from this page.

Split the clock the way the parts are weighted: \textbf{six minutes}, \textbf{ten minutes}, \textbf{fourteen minutes}. Start.

Stop when the time is up, even mid-word. An unfinished paper is information; an untimed one is not.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Now the rule this track states more sharply than any other, and the reason it does.

Latin is the language most people meet \textbf{only as reading}. Centuries of teaching it that way have made \textquotedblleft{}I know Latin\textquotedblright{} mean \textquotedblleft{}I can construe a page\textquotedblright{}, and a four-skill contract has to refuse that or it is not measuring the same thing at all.

So: each of the four papers is worth 25 points and \textbf{each must independently reach 15}. The aggregate must also reach 60 out of 100. Reading strength cannot hide absent writing. That is a project standard rather than an external certificate — Latin has no awarding body issuing one — and it is stated openly as this project's own choice.

Count your words against the three ranges. Being under the floor on any one of them is the same as not having attempted it.
\end{tcolorbox}
